country.name: Montenegro
country.tagline: Vranac country around Lake Skadar, the possible cradle of Zinfandel, and a wine cellar inside a Cold War aircraft tunnel.

stats.note: Wein.plus (2022): 2,825 ha of vineyard and 70,000 hl of wine; Wikipedia gives over 2,800 ha and 22,200 t of grapes in 2017.

country.overview:
Montenegro is small (about 2,800 ha of vines, roughly 70,000 hl a year) but it punches above its weight because of two grapes and one company. The grapes are Vranac, a deep-coloured, tannic red that makes up most of the country's wine, and Kratošija, a local name for the variety the world knows as Zinfandel or Primitivo; geneticists now consider Montenegro the most likely home of that grape, whose name as 'Cratosia' appears in the medieval Statute of Budva (1426 to 1442). Krstač is the native white, and Žižak and Kadarun are rarer reds.

The company is Plantaže 13. jul, founded in 1963 and still state-controlled, which planted the Ćemovsko polje plain south-east of Podgorica in the 1970s and 1980s into a single vineyard of more than 2,300 ha and some 11 million vines, one of the largest in Europe. It makes about 17 million bottles a year, led by Vranac Pro Corde and Crnogorski Vranac, and ages its premium wines in Šipčanik, a 356 m tunnel more than 30 m underground that was built as part of a military airfield and converted to a cellar in 2007.

Most vineyards lie in the basin of Lake Skadar, where the hot Zeta plain and the terraced slopes of Crmnica around Virpazar catch both Adriatic and continental influences; the Boka Kotorska and Budva-Bar coast and the cooler north make the rest. A legal decision of 2017 defines four wine regions and 15 subregions in line with EU practice, in preparation for EU membership.

history.title: Cratosia in the Statute of Budva
history.text: The medieval Statute of Budva mentions a grape called Cratosia, probably today's Kratošija, the earliest known record of the variety later identified as Zinfandel/Primitivo.

history.title: King Nikola's revival
history.text: Under Prince (later King) Nikola I viticulture recovered after Ottoman-era losses; Crmnica wine won first prizes at the 1907 Balkan Exhibition in London.

history.title: Plantaže and Ćemovsko polje
history.text: Plantaže was founded in 1963 with its first cellar at Lješkopolje; the Ćemovsko polje cellar opened in 1981 with 190,000 hl of capacity.

history.title: Šipčanik
history.text: In November 2007 Plantaže began ageing wine in Šipčanik, a 356 m tunnel more than 30 m underground in a former military facility of the airfield under the vineyard.

history.title: Wine regions defined
history.text: A government decision of October 2017 defined four wine-production regions and fifteen subregions.

country.classification: A 2017 government decision (Official Gazette 65/2017) defines four wine-production regions: the Montenegrin basin of Lake Skadar (subregions Kučki, Crmnički, Riječki, Podgorički, Piperski, Katunski, Bjelopavlićki), the Montenegrin coast (Boka Kotorska, Budva-Bar, Ulcinj, Adriatic hinterland), Nudo, and the Montenegrin north (Nikšićki, Bjelopoljski, Šćepan polje, Dragaljsko polje). No Montenegrin wine names were found in the EU or UK GI registers as of 2026.
country.climate_soils: The Skadar basin is hot, with Mediterranean summers and karst-limestone soils, gravels and terra rossa on the Zeta plain; Crmnica's terraces get Adriatic air over the coastal mountains. The coast is Mediterranean and the north continental.

grapes.name: Vranac
grapes.note: The national red, over 70% of production: deep colour, high tannin, black fruit.

grapes.name: Kratošija
grapes.note: Montenegro's name for Tribidrag/Zinfandel/Primitivo; dominant before phylloxera, now being replanted.

grapes.name: Krstač
grapes.note: Native white of the Podgorica area.

sources.title: FAOLEX/LEAP: Decision determining the regions for wine production (Montenegro, 2017)

regions.name: Lake Skadar Basin
regions.tagline: The Zeta plain, Ćemovsko polje and the terraces of Crmnica: Montenegro's Vranac heartland.
regions.summary: The Montenegrin basin of Lake Skadar is the main wine region, from the Zeta plain and Ćemovsko polje around Podgorica to the terraced slopes of Crmnica above Virpazar and the Riječki subregion around Rijeka Crnojevića. Plantaže's 2,300 ha vineyard dominates, but family wineries in Crmnica (Godinje, Virpazar) keep older traditions and Kratošija vines.
regions.history: Crmnica wine was considered the best in Montenegro in the 19th century and won prizes in London in 1907.
regions.terroir: Karst limestone, gravel and terra rossa; hot Mediterranean summers moderated by the lake.
regions.grapes: Vranac, Kratošija, Krstač, Žižak, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Chardonnay.

sources.title: FAOLEX/LEAP: Decision determining the regions for wine production (Montenegro, 2017)

regions.name: Montenegrin Coast
regions.tagline: Boka Kotorska to Ulcinj: small coastal vineyards above the Adriatic.
regions.summary: The coastal region runs from the Bay of Kotor through Budva and Bar to Ulcinj, with small vineyards on the slopes above the sea. Budva's medieval statute contains the first record of Kratošija.
regions.history: Venetian rule kept coastal vineyards alive during the Ottoman period.
regions.terroir: Limestone and flysch slopes; Mediterranean climate.
regions.styles: Reds and whites for local consumption.

sources.title: FAOLEX/LEAP: Decision determining the regions for wine production (Montenegro, 2017)

me-montenegrin-basin-of-skadar-lake.name: Montenegrin basin of Skadar Lake
me-montenegrin-basin-of-skadar-lake.summary: The main wine-production region defined by Montenegro's 2017 decision, covering the Lake Skadar basin with seven subregions: Kučki, Crmnički, Riječki, Podgorički, Piperski, Katunski and Bjelopavlićki. It includes Plantaže's Ćemovsko polje vineyard and the historic terraces of Crmnica, and produces most of the country's Vranac.

me-montenegrin-coast.name: Montenegrin coast
me-montenegrin-coast.summary: The coastal wine region defined in 2017, with four subregions: Boka Kotorska, Budva-Bar, Ulcinj and the Adriatic hinterland. Vineyards are small and scattered on terraces above the sea, and Venetian rule on this coast helped them survive the Ottoman centuries. Budva's medieval statute holds the first record of Kratošija.

me-montenegrin-north.name: Montenegrin north
me-montenegrin-north.summary: The northern wine region defined in 2017 has four subregions (Nikšićki, Bjelopoljski, Šćepan polje, Dragaljsko polje), with small vineyards in a cooler, continental climate. Most of the wine is made for home use, and the area is better known for the Trebjesa brewery at Nikšić than for wine.

me-nudo.name: Nudo
me-nudo.summary: Nudo is a small upland region near the Bosnian border north-west of Nikšić, defined as a separate wine-production region in 2017 without subregions. It is one of the most isolated vineyard areas in the country.

sites.name: Ćemovsko polje vineyard (Plantaže)
sites.text: South-east of Podgorica, Plantaže's single vineyard on the stony Ćemovsko polje covers more than 2,300 ha with some 11 million vines. It is one of the largest single vineyard blocks in Europe, planted mainly with Vranac, Kratošija, Krstač and international grapes.

sites.name: Šipčanik cellar
sites.text: Under Plantaže's Ćemovsko polje vineyard lies Šipčanik, a 356 m winding tunnel more than 30 m underground. It was built as a military facility of the former airfield. Since November 2007 it has held oak casks instead of aircraft: over 2 million litres of wine at 17 to 19 °C, plus an archive of 18,000 bottles.

sites.name: Virpazar and Crmnica
sites.text: Virpazar, on the shore of Lake Skadar, is the centre of Crmnica, whose terraced vineyards made Montenegro's most prized wine in the 19th century. Family cellars in Godinje and Limljani still make Vranac and Kratošija.

sites.name: Budva
sites.text: The walled town of Budva on the Adriatic gave its name to the medieval statute (1426 to 1442) that first records 'Cratosia', probably today's Kratošija. Geneticists now consider this the likely origin of Zinfandel.
